props.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: one must join the redemption blessing to the evening prayer (who does so is a son of the world to come)
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the prayers were instituted in the middle, between the two Shema recitations -- so no joining is required at evening
the seyag-baraita's clause: he recites the Shema and then prays -- Shema adjacent to the evening prayer
R' Yochanan's svara: redemption obtains at evening too, though full redemption only by morning -- so evening redemption can carry a joined prayer
RYbL's svara: since redemption is only from morning, the evening mention is not a redemption that requires joining
R' Yochanan's exposition: lying is compared to rising -- as at rising, Shema then prayer, so at lying
RYbL's exposition: as at rising the Shema is adjacent to one's bed, so at lying

schemas.gloss_en: as rising has Shema followed at once by prayer, so lying: at evening the Shema's redemption blessing is joined to the prayer

grounds.gloss_en: מתיב מר בריה דרבינא: at evening one blesses TWO after the Shema -- one must say hashkivenu, so redemption is NOT joined to prayer

answered_by.gloss_en: כיון דתקינו רבנן השכיבנו, כגאולה אריכתא דמיא -- hashkivenu counts as one long redemption blessing (just as ה' שפתי תפתח counts as part of a long prayer at morning, 4b.15)

schemas.gloss_en: as rising has the Shema adjacent to one's bed (first thing), so lying (last thing) -- the evening prayer was instituted earlier, in the middle

supports.gloss_en: מסייע ליה לרבי יוחנן -- the baraita has the Shema recited immediately before the evening prayer, as R' Yochanan requires
